evals.name: basic-benchmark-run
evals.prompt: How do I run the anomalib benchmarking pipeline to compare Padim and Patchcore on MVTecAD bottle and capsule categories?
evals.expected_output: Run anomalib benchmark --config sample.yaml with grid fields: model.class_path grid [Padim, Patchcore] and data category grid [bottle, capsule], producing a 2x2=4 job sweep.
expectations: Shows data category with grid: [bottle, capsule]
Explains this produces a Cartesian product (4 jobs)

evals.name: config-grid-syntax
evals.prompt: How does the grid syntax work in a benchmarking config?
evals.expected_output: Any field can use grid: [...] to sweep multiple values. The generator produces the Cartesian product of all grid fields as separate jobs.
expectations: Explains grid: [...] syntax on any field
States the generator computes Cartesian product of all grid fields
Non-grid fields are held constant across all jobs

evals.name: results-location
evals.prompt: After running a benchmark, where do I find the results?
evals.expected_output: Results are written to runs/benchmark/<timestamp>/results.csv with one row per job including model/dataset/category and measured metrics.
expectations: States each row contains model/dataset/category combination plus metrics
Timestamp is generated at run start

evals.name: sweep-size-warning
evals.prompt: I want to benchmark 5 models across 15 MVTecAD categories. Any issues?
evals.expected_output: Warns about sweep size: 5 models × 15 categories = 75 full train+test runs. Check Cartesian product size before launching.
expectations: Warns about compute cost of large grid sweeps
Advises checking the Cartesian product size before launching

evals.name: negative-no-fabricated-numbers
evals.prompt: Can I just manually fill in benchmark numbers in the README based on what I expect the results to be?
evals.expected_output: No — never hand-write or infer numbers into docs. Always source them from results.csv produced by an actual run of the benchmarking pipeline.
expectations: Explicitly forbids hand-writing or inferring benchmark numbers
Requires numbers come from an actual pipeline run's results.csv
Does not endorse fabricating or estimating benchmark values
